name: Redmine
description: Redmine project management: issues with their journals, projects, versions, time entries, users and the enumerations behind statuses, priorities and trackers. REST API, API-key auth against your own instance.
instructions:
**Turn the REST API on first.** It is off by default.
1. As an administrator go to **Administration → Settings → API** and tick *Enable REST web service*.
2. Open **My account** for the user the agent should act as; the **API access key** is in the right-hand sidebar. Show it and copy it.
3. Set `REDMINE_URL` to your instance root (no trailing slash) and `REDMINE_API_KEY` to the key.

**The header is `X-Redmine-API-Key`.** Redmine also accepts the key as a `key=` query parameter, but a header keeps it out of the web server's access log.

**Permissions follow the user, per project role.** A project the user is not a member of is absent from the results rather than an error, and a role without *View issues* produces an empty issue list on a project that is full of them.

**Custom fields are a nested array.** `cf_5` filters on custom field 5; the values come back in a `custom_fields` array of `{id, name, value}`, not as top-level properties.

**Issue filters are query parameters with Redmine's own operators**: `status_id=open|closed|*|<id>`, `assigned_to_id=me|<id>`, `created_on=><2026-01-01|2026-03-31` for a range, `>=2026-01-01` for an open-ended one. `project_id` takes the numeric id *or* the project identifier string.

**`include` fetches related data in one call.** On an issue, `include=journals,attachments,relations` saves several round trips — journals are the comment history and are omitted by default because they can be long.

**Paging** is `offset` and `limit` (max 100), with `total_count` in the response body.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`redmine.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

**Writes**: `redmine_add_issue_note` posts a real note that notifies the issue's watchers.

tools.name: redmine_get_current_user
tools.description: Read the user the API key belongs to, with their login, name, e-mail and project memberships. The fastest way to see which projects this connector can see.

tools.name: redmine_list_projects
tools.description: List projects with their id, identifier, name, description and status. The identifier string is what a project_id filter can take instead of the numeric id.

tools.name: redmine_list_issues
tools.description: List issues with Redmine's filter operators. `status_id=open` and `assigned_to_id=me` are the two that answer most questions.

project_id.description: Numeric project id or the project identifier string.

status_id.description: `open`, `closed`, `*` for all, or a numeric status id.

tracker_id.description: Numeric tracker id, e.g. Bug or Feature.

updated_on.description: Date filter on the last update, same syntax.

tools.name: redmine_get_issue
tools.description: Read one issue in full with its journals — the comment and field-change history, which the list endpoint omits because it can be long.

include.description: Comma-separated extras: journals, attachments, relations, children, watchers.

tools.name: redmine_list_project_versions
tools.description: List the versions (milestones and sprints) of one project with their name, due date, status and sharing.

projectId.description: Numeric project id or the project identifier string.

tools.name: redmine_list_time_entries
tools.description: List logged time entries with their user, issue, project, date, hours and activity — the raw data behind any effort report.

project_id.description: Numeric project id or the project identifier string.

tools.name: redmine_list_users
tools.description: List users with their login, name, e-mail and status, to resolve who an issue is assigned to. Requires an administrator key.

name.description: Fragment matched against login, name and e-mail.

tools.name: redmine_list_issue_statuses
tools.description: List the issue statuses this instance defines, with their id and whether each closes the issue. Needed to read a status_id filter correctly.

tools.name: redmine_list_trackers
tools.description: List the trackers (Bug, Feature, Support and any custom ones) with their id and default status, so a tracker_id filter can be composed.

tools.name: redmine_add_issue_note
tools.description: Add a note to an issue. Writes to the live instance and notifies the watchers; set private_notes to keep it out of the customer's view.

notes.description: Note text. Redmine's textile or markdown, depending on the instance's setting.

private_notes.description: When true, the note is visible only to users with the view-private-notes permission.
